paragraphs.title: The Queen of Sheba’s Visit and Her Impression of Solomon’s Wisdom

easy.explanation: The queen of Sheba came to prove Solomon with hard questions.
easy.q: Who came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions?

easy.explanation: Her camels carried spices, much gold, and precious stones.
easy.q: What did the camels of the queen of Sheba carry?

easy.explanation: She gave Solomon gold, spices, and precious stones.
easy.q: What did the queen of Sheba give Solomon?

answers: To hear and test his wisdom
To build a palace in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: She heard of Solomon’s fame and came to prove him with hard questions.
medium.q: Why did the queen of Sheba come to Solomon?

answers: Only the amount of gold in the palace
Solomon’s answers, house, table, servants, and royal order
Only the number of Solomon’s horses
medium.explanation: She saw Solomon’s wisdom, house, table, servants, apparel, and royal arrangements.
medium.q: What especially impressed the queen of Sheba?

medium.explanation: The expression describes her great amazement at what she saw.
medium.q: What does the statement that there was “no more spirit in her” mean?

answers: She saw for herself that reality exceeded the report
She refused to speak with Solomon
challenge.explanation: She said she had not believed the report until her own eyes had seen it.
challenge.q: How did the queen of Sheba confirm that Solomon’s reputation was trustworthy?

answers: His kingship was connected with doing judgment and justice
Wisdom caused him to leave the throne
challenge.explanation: She blessed the Lord for making Solomon king to do judgment and justice.
challenge.q: What connection did the queen of Sheba make between Solomon’s wisdom and his kingship?

answers: He answered all her questions completely
He hid his wisdom from her
challenge.explanation: The passage says there was nothing hidden from the king that he did not tell her.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Solomon’s response to the queen’s questions?

paragraphs.title: Gold, Algum Wood, and Royal Wealth

easy.explanation: The yearly amount was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold.
easy.q: How many talents of gold came to Solomon in one year?

easy.explanation: Solomon made a throne of ivory and overlaid it with the best gold.
easy.q: What was Solomon’s throne made of?

easy.explanation: The navy of Tharshish came once in three years.
easy.q: How often did the navy of Tharshish come?

medium.explanation: The algum trees were used for pillars, harps, and psalteries.
medium.q: What did Solomon make from the algum trees?

answers: Gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks
medium.explanation: The navy brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
medium.q: What cargo did the navy of Tharshish bring?

medium.explanation: A target was a large shield made of beaten gold.
medium.q: What is a “target” in this passage?

answers: Dependence on the queen of Sheba
challenge.explanation: The ivory, gold, steps, and lions display unusual royal splendor.
challenge.q: What does the description of Solomon’s throne emphasize about his wealth and status?

answers: Silver was considered of little value because of the great abundance
Solomon forbade the use of silver
challenge.explanation: Silver was treated as insignificant because Solomon had so much of it.
challenge.q: What does the statement that silver was “nothing accounted of” mean?

answers: Solomon’s kingdom displayed unique wealth and magnificence
Solomon did not use the throne
challenge.explanation: The statement presents the throne as unmatched among other kingdoms.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that no such throne was made in any kingdom?

paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Renown and the Gifts of the Nations

easy.explanation: Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
easy.q: In what was Solomon greater than all the kings of the earth?

easy.explanation: People came to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
easy.q: Why did people from all the earth seek Solomon?

answers: Vessels, garments, armour, spices, horses, and mules
easy.explanation: They brought many kinds of gifts year by year.
easy.q: What did visitors bring Solomon each year?

answers: They wanted to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart
They needed to buy cedar from him
medium.explanation: The passage directly connects their coming with God-given wisdom.
medium.q: What caused people from all the earth to seek Solomon?

answers: They were brought year by year
medium.explanation: The gifts were brought at a rate year by year.
medium.q: Which detail shows that the gifts were regular rather than one-time offerings?

medium.explanation: A present is a gift brought to Solomon.
medium.q: What does “his present” mean in this context?

answers: Both attracted people and gifts to him
Wisdom prevented him from becoming wealthy
Wealth caused him to lose his wisdom
challenge.explanation: People came for his wisdom, and they brought valuable gifts.
challenge.q: What relationship between Solomon’s wisdom and wealth appears in the passage?

answers: Solomon’s connections involved many kinds of goods
challenge.explanation: The gifts included vessels, clothing, armour, spices, horses, and mules.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the wide variety of gifts?

answers: God put it in his heart
He learned it only from Egyptian merchants
It came from the size of his army
challenge.explanation: The passage says that God had put the wisdom in his heart.
challenge.q: How is the source of Solomon’s wisdom described?

paragraphs.title: The Chariot Army and Abundance in Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Solomon had a thousand and four hundred chariots.
easy.q: How many chariots did Solomon have?
How many horsemen did Solomon have?

easy.explanation: The king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones.
easy.q: How is silver described as being in Jerusalem?

answers: Only in the house of the forest of Lebanon
In the cities for chariots and with the king at Jerusalem
medium.explanation: He placed them in the chariot cities and kept some with him at Jerusalem.
medium.q: Where did Solomon place the chariots and horsemen?

medium.explanation: The comparison emphasizes the enormous amount of silver.
medium.q: What does the comparison of silver to stones communicate?

medium.explanation: The context shows that these cities were used to station chariots.

answers: Military power together with material abundance
challenge.explanation: The verses describe both chariots and horsemen and abundant silver and wood.
challenge.q: What combination is portrayed in Solomon’s kingdom?

answers: That cedar was used only for ships
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes that cedar was plentiful in Solomon’s kingdom.
challenge.q: What does the comparison of cedars to sycomore trees in the vale emphasize?

answers: Jerusalem was the king’s center, while part of the force was stationed in chariot cities
All the forces were kept only in Jerusalem
The chariot cities were outside Solomon’s kingdom
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes the chariot cities from the horsemen kept with the king at Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What relationship between Jerusalem and the chariot cities appears in the passage?

easy.explanation: Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt.
easy.q: From where were Solomon’s horses brought?

easy.explanation: The king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.
easy.q: Who received the linen yarn at a price?

answers: The kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria
easy.explanation: They were brought by their means to the kings of the Hittites and Syria.
easy.q: To whom were the chariots and horses also supplied?

answers: They received goods at a price and managed the royal trade
medium.explanation: The king’s merchants handled the goods received at a price.
medium.q: What role did the king’s merchants play in the trade described?

answers: One hundred fifty shekels of silver
medium.explanation: A chariot cost six hundred shekels of silver.
medium.q: What was the price of a chariot brought out of Egypt?

answers: One hundred fifty shekels of silver
medium.explanation: A horse cost an hundred and fifty shekels of silver.
medium.q: What was the price of a horse?

answers: The horses were used only in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Selling to the Hittite and Syrian kings shows international regional trade.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the sale of chariots and horses to other kings?

answers: Every king set a random price
challenge.explanation: The passage gives specific prices for chariots and horses.
challenge.q: What do the stated prices suggest about the trade?

answers: They show royal control of a horse-and-chariot trade
They cancel the earlier description of wealth
They describe only a private gift
challenge.explanation: The organized trade in horses and chariots demonstrates Solomon’s economic power.
challenge.q: How do these verses add to the description of Solomon’s wealth?
